activities.title: State is local to a component instance

content.title: State is local to a component instance
content.text:
If the same component is rendered twice, each copy can have its own state.

That means:

```jsx
<Status />
<Status />
```

creates two independent pieces of component memory.

content.title: Hook rule
content.text:
A Hook such as `useState` should be called at the top level of the component, not inside a condition or loop.

Why?

React relies on the stable order of Hook calls across renders.

content.question: What is the strongest reason to use state instead of a regular variable for interactive UI data?

options.text: State variables are shorter to type.
State lets React remember the value between renders and update the UI when it changes.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. State lets React remember the value between renders and update the UI when it changes.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. State lets React remember the value between renders and update the UI when it changes.

takeaways: **Mental model:** State is component memory connected to rendering.
**Senior habit:** When a UI value changes over time, ask whether React needs to remember it and re-render from it. That is a strong signal that the value belongs in state.
